title: Trailing clouds of glory
hookLine: a Christian poet seems to say the soul lived before birth; we come trailing clouds of glory (Intimations Ode)
tomorrow: some moments come back for years. do they heal you, or haunt you?

lines: WHERE WAS I BEFORE I WAS BORN?
BIRTH IS A SLEEP AND A FORGETTING.
cards: Kids ask the questions grown-ups quietly stopped asking. Where was I before I was born? Wordsworth's answer comes in a long ode, and it's a puzzle.
"Our birth is but a sleep and a forgetting", he writes. Birth as falling asleep? Then: "The Soul that rises with us, our life's Star, / Hath had elsewhere its setting, / And cometh from afar".
A Christian poet, saying the soul was somewhere before birth? Churches have long rejected that idea. So what is he doing?

teach.h: A POET'S NOTION, NOT A CREED.
teach.b: Wordsworth answered the puzzle himself, in a note he dictated years later. He didn't mean to teach that the soul lived before birth.
It was an old notion, he said, and he used it as a poet, because it fit something he knew from childhood. The old notion is Plato's.
In the dialogues called the Meno and the Phaedo, Socrates argues that learning is really remembering, anamnesis: the soul knew the truth before birth and forgot it on arrival.

teach.h: FROM GOD, WHO IS OUR HOME.
teach.b: Wordsworth borrows the picture, then, a few lines on, turns it toward his own faith: "But trailing clouds of glory do we come / From God, who is our home: / Heaven lies about us in our infancy!"

Then the growing up: "Shades of the prison-house begin to close / Upon the growing Boy", until the light fades "into the light of common day." So here's the solution. It isn't a doctrine of past lives.
It's a picture of a teaching Christians do hold: we come from God, and we go home to God. Ecclesiastes says it plainly: "the spirit shall return unto God who gave it."
Wordsworth borrows Plato to explain why a child sees glory that grown-ups miss. And the ode doesn't end in loss. He says he will grieve not, but find strength in what remains behind.

how: Christians teach that each soul comes from God and returns to God; Wordsworth's ode borrows that picture, and he called its soul-before-birth idea a poet's notion.

games.q: what does “trailing clouds of glory” mean?
o: the bright mist that hangs over a summer morning
a hero's victory parade through the city streets
children arriving from God with heaven still on them

games.q: the child and the glory: tap the pairs.
p: what closes on the growing boy
the spirit returns to God who gave it

s: Wordsworth said he meant to teach that the soul lived before birth
in a later note he called it an old notion he used as a poet, not a belief he meant to teach.
Plato's Socrates argues that learning is a kind of remembering
anamnesis: the soul knew the truth before birth and forgets it on arrival.
the ode ends in hopeless grief for childhood's lost light
it finds strength in what remains behind.

games.q: a friend says Wordsworth's ode proves he believed in past lives. what's the best reply from today?
o: he said it was an old notion from Plato that he used as a poet, not a belief he taught.
yes; the ode says plainly that every soul is reborn again and again.
no; the ode has nothing about the soul before birth in it at all.
games.why: the ode does say our birth is a sleep and a forgetting, and Wordsworth's own note calls that a poet's use of an old notion. the line it lands on is Christian: from God, who is our home.

practice: Say out loud, quietly, one thing that amazed you as a small child: a snowfall, a beetle, a grandparent's hands. Describe it in a few sentences, as if to someone who has never seen one. Then sit with whatever light comes back.

wordCard.voice: Trailing clouds of glory: Wordsworth's picture of children arriving from God with heaven still around them. A poet's notion, he said, not a creed.

orig.note: Greek: recollection, remembering. Plato's word for learning as the soul remembering what it knew before birth.

carryVoice: Keep this: trailing clouds of glory, from God, who is our home. Till next time.
